title: Small Caps Enter Correction, Market Breadth Warnings (Russell 2000)
summary: Gotrade News - The Russell 2000 small-cap index has fallen more than 10% from its recent peak and entered correction territory, as fears over rising
body_markdown:
The gap shows up in the large-cap benchmarks. Per StoneX market analyst David Scutt, writing for[StoneX](https://www.stonex.com/en-gb/news-and-analysis/russell-2000-breaks-200-day-average-as-cpi-risk-looms/) , Russell 2000 futures fell close to 9% from mid-August to the morning of the CPI report, while Nasdaq 100 and S&P 500 futures posted small gains over the same period. Those are the indexes behind the[SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/spy/) and the[Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/qqq/) .


## Russell 2000 Closes Below Its 200-Day Average


Scutt wrote that "US small-cap equities have struggled since hitting record highs in August," and noted the index closed below its 200-day moving average on Tuesday, October 13. He flagged a support zone around 2,800, made up of the uptrend from the April 2025 lows, the 200-day average and horizontal support.


Below that zone, Scutt pointed to the October 7 intraday low of 2,761.6, then 2,720 and 2,560 as the next levels on the[stock chart](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/how-to-read-a-stock-chart/) . On the upside he named downtrend resistance at 2,840, the October 6 high of 2,869.4, and the 50-day and 100-day moving averages around 2,924 to 2,938.


## Why Are Rising Rates Hitting Small Caps Harder?


According to StoneX, small caps have become unusually sensitive to bond yields, with the Russell 2000 moving sharply in the opposite direction to US Treasury yields by historical standards.


> "The Russell 2000's relationship with US Treasury yields has become extremely negative by historical standards." David Scutt, StoneX


TokenPost added that inflation worries and concerns about higher interest rates weigh on smaller and cyclical stocks in particular. Seeking Alpha also noted signs of trouble developing beneath the surface of the market, beyond the selloff in large technology names.
